scope: Proposition 3.7 (An elliptic cone containing the projected trap) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose G′ = 1 throughout the photon region. The union of the spatial projections of both trapped null sheets is contained, with a positive margin, in a spatial conic neighborhood T with compact base support separated from the horizon and from both spatial ends of the estimates. On this neighborhood, bij (y)ηiηj ≥ c|η|2 (3.28) for some c > 0 and any fixed auxiliary cotangent norm on the compact base support. Both temporal roots there are nonzero and have absolute values comparable to |η|. One can choose nested smaller and larger conic neighborhoods with these properties, and the same choices work after sufficiently small changes of exact Kerr parameters and stationary charts.
